A.notes: Site A is clear, calm, and competent, with all required content present and a friendly illustrated mangrove motif. But the idea is fairly conventional public-interest web design, and the section cards/forms feel generic rather than authored. Motion is hard to judge from stills, but nothing in the layout suggests it plays a storytelling role; reduced-motion handling and accessibility checks are strong.

B.notes: Site B has a strong single idea carried throughout: the site behaves like a measured field document/building stack, with floors, counting, roots, and the 140-hectare figure all integrated into the visual language. The bilingual typography is far more distinctive and confident than A, and the 140-dot graphic is an excellent factual device. I am slightly cautious on access/performance because the interface is denser and more experimental, but the measured checks pass and reduced-motion screenshots show proper fallback.

raw.why: B is the rarer design: it turns the brief into a coherent, memorable visual system without inventing facts, while A is solid but much more template-like.
